items.title: Lifted State Policy Optimization: Internalizing Self-Correction through Transition Geometry
items.summary_1line: Preference optimization ranks final answers and trajectory RL maximizes aggregate returns, yet neither credits the local change that turns a flawed reasoning state into a better one. We introduce Lifted State Policy O...
items.editor_note: Introduces Lifted State Policy Optimization, crediting the local change from a flawed reasoning state to a better one.

items.title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces

items.title: How Deterministic SAST and AI Security Agents Divide the Work: Coverage, Harness Policy and Cost in Snyk VulnBench 2.0
items.summary_1line: We ask what AI coding agents and AI security harnesses find that deterministic static application security testing (SAST) does not, and what they miss that SAST catches. VulnBench 2.0 is a benchmark of 108 hand-curate...
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agent, harness, eval.
items.editor_note: Benchmarks what AI security agents find and miss versus deterministic SAST, including harness policy and cost.

editorial.tldr: On Oct 14 a paper proposed Lifted State Policy Optimization to credit the local change that turns a flawed reasoning state into a better one. ReflectPO (Oct 22) and SOPO (Oct 23) then applied policy optimization to long-horizon agents and hallucination detection.
editorial.whats_new: Snyk VulnBench 2.0 (Oct 28) compares deterministic SAST with AI security agents on 108 hand-curated cases, reporting coverage, harness policy and cost, after papers framing the policy as part of the harness.
editorial.why_it_matters: The thread shifts from training the policy to the interface around it: the harness and policy together decide agent behavior, so harness changes need their own evals.
editorial.take_for_builders: Treat these as preprints: before changing a training pipeline, wait for code and replication; meanwhile, rerun your agent evals whenever the harness changes, not only the model.

beats.headline: Lifted State Policy Optimization targets self-correction
Reflection-guided and multiscale optimization for long-horizon agents
Policy and harness are treated as one system
VulnBench 2.0 measures harness policy and cost against deterministic SAST

open_questions: Do any of these methods publish code or reproducible results on public benchmarks?
Does VulnBench 2.0 get run by anyone outside Snyk's authors?
Do harness-aware evaluations change reported rankings of agents versus bare-model scores?
